sourceNote: Topic and subtopic headings transcribed from the publicly available syllabus structure; verify against the current official document. Learning-objective statements are our own paraphrase of the syllabus content, and their numbering is ours, not the board's (subtopic code + .n; topic code + .0.n where no subtopic headings are recorded).
notes: Source status (checked 2026-10-07): the official Ministry PDF 'Mathematics Syllabus Forms 1-4, 2015-2022' could not be opened (the provincial copy at https://www.mopsemashwest.gov.zw/files/Mathematics%20Syllabus.pdf has an expired TLS certificate; other copies are behind document-sharing sites). The fourteen topics and the subtopics recorded here are corroborated by secondary summaries of that syllabus and by the predecessor official ZIMSEC syllabus 'O Level Mathematics 4008/4028, for examination in November 2012-2017'. Verify every heading, and replace the officialDocument URL with the exact syllabus download address once confirmed.

Version dates: the predecessor syllabus 4008/4028 was examined up to November 2017, so this syllabus is assumed to be first examined in November 2018 (effectiveFrom 2018-01-01). Confirm the subject code 4004 and the last examination year, and create a new version file for the Heritage-Based Curriculum syllabus when it replaces this one.
The syllabus covers Forms 1 to 4; the O-Level examination at the end of Form 4 assumes all of it. Nodes are not split by form.

Subtopic wording in Topic 1 ('Approximations and estimations', 'Ratios, rates and proportions', 'Scales and simple map problems') comes from a secondary summary of the 2015-2022 syllabus; 1.6 Scales and simple map problems also appears in the predecessor syllabus (6.1.7). Confirm the exact wording and numbering.

Topics 2 Sets, 6 Variation, 9 Statistics, 11 Vectors, 12 Matrices, 13 Transformation and 14 Probability are recorded without subtopics because their subtopic headings could not be confirmed. Their content is recorded in objectives coded n.0.k; add subtopics when the official headings are confirmed (a new structure must be decided before this version is published).

8.7 Circle properties: circle theorems are in the syllabus (predecessor 6.7.4 'Circles'; secondary summaries list circle theorems in Form 4 Geometry), but the heading and position of this subtopic are not confirmed. Tangent and chord properties beyond those listed in the predecessor (radius, diameter, chord, tangent, cyclic quadrilateral) should be checked.

1.1 number patterns and 5.1 functional notation appear in secondary summaries of the 2015-2022 syllabus but not in the predecessor; only linear patterns (math.algebra.sequences) and function notation (math.algebra.functions) are covered, not the Cambridge-only non-linear sequences or inverse and composite functions. Confirm.

Matrices that represent transformations are covered under 13 Transformation (the predecessor had 'Matrices as operators' under Transformations); a secondary summary lists them under Matrices in Form 4. Confirm the placement.

Not covered for ZIMSEC because they could not be confirmed in this syllabus (Cambridge-only concepts of the family): calculator use, surds beyond recognising irrational numbers, non-linear sequences, simultaneous equations with one non-linear equation, conversion graphs, sketching curves, differentiation, inverse and composite functions, length and midpoint of a line segment, perpendicular lines, exact trigonometric values, graphs of trigonometric functions, scatter diagrams and conditional probability. The predecessor also had estimating the area under a curve and finding turning points from graphs; confirm whether they remain.

Statistics: the predecessor and secondary summaries list frequency tables, bar and pie charts, histograms, frequency polygons, averages of grouped data (including an assumed mean) and cumulative frequency (quartiles, interquartile and semi-interquartile range). Confirm whether histograms have unequal class widths.

Assessment: two written papers. The predecessor 4008/4028 had Paper 1 (2 h 30 min, about 30 short-answer questions, no calculators or tables) and Paper 2 (2 h 30 min; Section A six compulsory structured questions, Section B three questions from six), each 50%. Durations, marks, weightings, calculator rules and any school-based continuous assessment for 4004 are deliberately not recorded until confirmed from the official document.

Objective statements are recorded only for content confirmed by the predecessor syllabus or the secondary summaries. 7.2.1-7.2.5 keep the codes already referenced by the existing quadratic-equations content.
overview: ZIMSEC O-Level Mathematics builds number sense, algebraic and geometric reasoning, measurement, financial literacy, statistics and probability, and the confidence to use them in everyday life, further study and work in Zimbabwe. The syllabus runs from Form 1 to Form 4 and is examined at the end of Form 4.
assessmentOverview: The syllabus is examined by two written papers, Paper 1 and Paper 2. Confirm durations, marks and calculator rules in the official document.

objectives.text: Identify and use natural numbers, integers, even, odd and prime numbers, rational and irrational numbers, and square and cube numbers.
Find factors, multiples, prime factorisations, highest common factors and lowest common multiples of whole numbers.
Convert between common fractions, decimals and percentages and use them in context.
Calculate percentages of quantities and percentage increases and decreases.
Order numbers and use the symbols =, ≠, >, <, ≥ and ≤.
Apply the four operations and the order of operations, including brackets, to whole numbers, fractions, decimals and directed numbers, and use directed numbers in practical situations.
Find squares, square roots, cubes and cube roots of numbers.
Recognise, continue and describe number patterns.
Round numbers to a given number of decimal places or significant figures and to a sensible accuracy for a problem.
Estimate quantities and the results of calculations.
Find upper and lower bounds of values given to a stated accuracy, and of the results of simple calculations with them such as the area of a rectangle.
Simplify ratios and divide quantities in a given ratio.
Solve problems on direct and inverse proportion, including by the unitary method.
Calculate with rates such as speed and cost per unit.
Write numbers in standard form A × 10ⁿ, where 1 ≤ A < 10 and n is an integer, and convert them to ordinary form.
Add, subtract, multiply and divide numbers in standard form.
State the place value of digits in numbers written in bases two to ten.
Convert numbers from one base to another.
Add and subtract numbers in bases other than ten.
Find the scale of a map or drawing from given information and write it as a ratio or representative fraction.
Use a given scale to calculate actual distances and areas from a map or drawing.
Describe sets by listing their elements, in words and in set-builder notation.
Use set notation for elements, the number of elements, the universal set, the empty set, complements, subsets, unions and intersections.
Use Venn diagrams with up to three sets to represent sets and solve problems.
Interpret household bills, bank statements, wages and budgets and solve problems on them.
Calculate simple interest and compound interest.
Solve problems on profit and loss, discount, commission and hire purchase.
Calculate sales tax or value added tax, income tax and customs and excise duty from given rates.
Convert between currencies using given exchange rates.
Calculate the depreciation of an item's value over time.
Use SI units of length, mass, area, volume and capacity in practical situations and convert between larger and smaller units, including the hectare.
Read and calculate with times on the 12-hour and 24-hour clocks.
Calculate the perimeter and area of rectangles, triangles, parallelograms, trapezia, circles and combined shapes.
Calculate arc lengths and the areas of sectors and segments of circles.
Calculate surface areas and volumes of cuboids, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones and spheres.
Use density to calculate mass or volume.
Use functional notation f(x) and evaluate functions for given values.
Draw straight-line graphs, find gradients from two points, and interpret and obtain equations of the form y = mx + c, including recognising parallel lines.
Construct tables of values and draw graphs of linear, quadratic, cubic and inverse functions, reading off values and turning points.
Solve equations graphically, including from the points of intersection of two graphs.
Estimate the gradient of a curve at a point by drawing a tangent and interpret it as a rate of change.
Draw and interpret distance–time (displacement–time) graphs.
Draw and interpret speed–time (velocity–time) graphs, and calculate acceleration and distance travelled from them.
Express direct and inverse variation algebraically, find the constant of variation and solve problems.
Express joint and partial variation algebraically and solve problems.
Sketch and interpret graphs of direct, inverse and partial variation.
Write algebraic expressions and formulae from words and substitute values into them.
Expand and simplify algebraic expressions, including products of two binomials.
Factorise expressions using common factors, grouping, the difference of two squares and quadratic trinomials.
Find the HCF and LCM of algebraic expressions and simplify, add, subtract, multiply and divide algebraic fractions.
Change the subject of a formula.
Solve linear equations in one unknown, including equations with fractions.
Solve simultaneous linear equations in two unknowns by substitution and by elimination.
Solve quadratic equations by factorising.
Solve quadratic equations by completing the square and by using the quadratic formula.
Form equations from practical situations, solve them and interpret the solutions.
Solve linear inequalities, including simultaneous inequalities, and show the solutions on a number line.
Represent linear inequalities in two variables as regions on a graph.
Use simple linear programming to find the maximum or minimum value of a quantity in a region defined by inequalities.
Use the laws of indices, including zero, negative and fractional indices, to simplify and evaluate expressions.
Solve simple equations in which the unknown is an index.
Use the relationship between indices and logarithms and the laws of logarithms to simplify and evaluate expressions and solve simple equations.
Use the language of points, lines and angles, including types of angle and complementary and supplementary angles.
Calculate angles at a point, on a straight line, vertically opposite and formed by parallel lines and a transversal, giving reasons.
Solve problems involving angles of elevation and depression.
Describe directions using three-figure bearings and compass bearings.
Solve problems on bearings and distances by scale drawing and by calculation.
Use the properties of triangles and special quadrilaterals.
Calculate interior and exterior angles of polygons and the number of sides of a regular polygon.
Name polygons with up to ten sides.
Identify similar and congruent figures and use the conditions for congruent triangles.
Solve problems using scale factors for the lengths and areas of similar figures and the volumes and masses of similar solids.
Construct triangles, quadrilaterals and other polygons using a ruler and compasses (and a protractor where needed), and make scale drawings.
Construct perpendicular bisectors, angle bisectors, perpendiculars from or at a point, and angles of 30°, 45°, 60° and 90° with a ruler and compasses only.
Construct and use the loci of points equidistant from two points or two lines, or at a fixed distance from a point or a line.
Identify lines of symmetry and the order of rotational symmetry of plane shapes.
Relate the properties of triangles, quadrilaterals, regular polygons and circles to their symmetry.
Use the properties of radii, diameters, chords and tangents of a circle.
Use the circle theorems on the angle at the centre, the angle in a semicircle, angles in the same segment, cyclic quadrilaterals and the alternate segment to calculate angles, giving reasons.
Collect, classify and tabulate data, including grouped data in frequency tables.
Draw, read and interpret bar charts, pie charts, histograms, frequency polygons and frequency tables, and draw simple inferences from them.
Calculate the mean, median, mode and range of data, use an assumed mean where appropriate, and identify the modal class of grouped data.
Draw cumulative frequency curves and use them to estimate the median, quartiles, interquartile range and semi-interquartile range.
Use Pythagoras' theorem to find sides of right-angled triangles and recognise Pythagorean triples.
Use sine, cosine and tangent to find sides and angles of right-angled triangles.
Use the sine, cosine and tangent of obtuse angles.
Use the sine rule and the cosine rule to solve triangles.
Use the formula area = ½ab sin C to find the area of a triangle.
Solve three-dimensional problems, including finding the angle between a line and a plane.
Represent translations by column vectors and directed line segments, and recognise equal, negative, parallel and position vectors.
Add and subtract vectors, multiply a vector by a scalar and calculate the magnitude of a vector.
Use vectors to establish properties of plane shapes, such as parallel lines and collinear points.
Use a matrix to store information and state its order.
Add and subtract matrices, multiply a matrix by a scalar, and multiply matrices of order up to 2 × 2.
Find the determinant of a 2 × 2 matrix, distinguish singular from non-singular matrices and find the inverse of a non-singular 2 × 2 matrix.
Use the inverse of a 2 × 2 matrix to solve a pair of simultaneous linear equations.
Translate, reflect, rotate and enlarge plane figures and describe these transformations fully.
Carry out and describe one-way and two-way stretches and shears with the axes as invariant lines.
Identify and use 2 × 2 matrices that represent transformations, including combinations of transformations.
Use the language of probability, including random, certain, impossible, sample space, equally likely, mutually exclusive and independent events.
Distinguish between experimental and theoretical probability and calculate the probability of a single event.
Calculate probabilities of combined events using outcome tables, tree diagrams and the rules for mutually exclusive and independent events.
